column3: NKJV names “Jesus,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “He Himself stood.”
NKJV has “in your hearts,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the singular “in your heart.”
NKJV includes “and some honeycomb,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has only “a piece of broiled fish.”
NKJV includes “and thus it was necessary,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “Thus it is written, that the Christ should suffer.”
NKJV has “repentance and remission of sins,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “repentance for the forgiveness of sins.”
NKJV includes “of Jerusalem,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “in the city.”
NKJV includes “praising and” and the final “Amen,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “blessing God.”
